'''''Analysis''''' is a [[Peer review|peer-reviewed]] [[academic journal]] of [[philosophy]] established in 1933 that is published quarterly by [[Oxford University Press]] on behalf of the Analysis Trust.<ref>{{cite web |title=Analysis {{!}} About the Journal |url=https://academic.oup.com/analysis/pages/About |website=Oxford Academic |access-date=18 August 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Welcome to the Analysis Trust |url=http://www.analysistrust.org/society/analysis/ |website=The Analysis Trust |access-date=18 August 2019}}</ref> Prior to January 2009, the journal was published by [[Wiley-Blackwell|Blackwell Publishing]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20081221215939/http://www.nottingham.ac.uk/journals/analysis/analysis_journal/news.htm Analysis Journal: News] (Accessed 07-01-2009)</ref> Electronic access to this journal is available via [[JSTOR]] (1933–2013), [[John Wiley & Sons|Wiley InterScience]] (1996–2008), and [[Oxford University Press|Oxford Journals]] (2009–present).<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130105081655/http://www3.interscience.wiley.com/journal/118517170/home|title=Wiley-Blackwell InterScience, ''Analysis''}}</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20081218172220/http://analysis.oxfordjournals.org/ Oxford Journals, ''Analysis'']</ref> The journal publishes short, concise articles (of up to 4000 words, excluding bibliography) in virtually any field of the [[Analytic philosophy|analytic]] tradition.

The journal was founded in 1933 by philosophers from Oxford, Cambridge, and London, who were influenced by the views and methods of philosophers like [[Bertrand Russell]], [[G.E. Moore]], and [[Ludwig Wittgenstein]]. Its first issued appeared in November of that year.<ref>{{cite book |editor1-last=MacDonald |editor1-first=Margaret |title=Philosophy and Analysis |date=1966 |publisher=Basil Blackwell |page=1 |url=https://archive.org/details/philosophyanalys0000macd/page/n9/mode/2up |chapter=Introduction}}</ref>

== Editors ==
* 1933–1948: [[Austin Duncan-Jones]]
* 1948–1956: [[Margaret MacDonald (philosopher)|Margaret MacDonald]]
* 1956–1965: [[Bernard Mayo]]
* 1965–1971: [[Peter Winch]]
* 1971–1976: [[C. J. F. Williams]]
* 1976–1987: Christopher Kirwan
* 1987–1999: Peter Smith
* 2000–2016: Michael Clark
* 2016–2017: Chris Daly and David Liggins
* 2017–2021: [[David Liggins]]
* 2021–2024: David Liggins, Stacie Friend, and Lee Walters
* 2024–present: Stacie Friend, Lee Walters, and Roger Clark

== Noteworthy articles ==
A number of noteworthy works by notable authors have been published in the journal. These include{

* [[Stephen Toulmin|Toulmin, Stephen]]. (1948). "The Logical Status of Psycho-Analysis". '''9''' (2), pp.&nbsp;23–29.
* [[Alonzo Church|Church, Alonzo]]. (1950). "On Carnap's Analysis of Statements of Assertion and Belief". '''10''' (5), pp.&nbsp;97–99.
* [[Alan Ross Anderson|Anderson, Alan Ross]]. (1951). "A Note on Subjunctive and Counterfactual Conditionals". '''12''' (2), pp.&nbsp;35–38.
* [[Nuel Belnap]]. (1962) "Tonk, Plonk and Plink". '''22''' (6) pp.&nbsp;130–134.
* [[Edmund Gettier|Gettier, Edmund]]. (1963). "[[Is Justified True Belief Knowledge?]]". '''23''' (6), pp.&nbsp;121–123.
* [[David Lewis (philosopher)|Lewis, David]]. (1988). "Vague Identity: Evans Misunderstood". '''48''' (3), pp.&nbsp;128–130.
* [[Andy Clark|Clark, Andy]] and [[David Chalmers|Chalmers, David]]. (1998). "The Extended Mind". '''58''' (1), pp.&nbsp;7–19.
* [[Joshua Knobe|Knobe, Joshua]]. (2003). "Intentional Action and Side Effects in Ordinary Language". '''63''' (279), pp.&nbsp;190–194.
